name: FactorAlpha
short: An end-to-end quantitative stock recommendation platform: a data pipeline, a five-factor rating model, and the product API behind factoralpha.ai. Three tiers, 5,000+ US equities.
tags:
Python · FastAPI · Azure SQL
PostgreSQL · pandas · React
sub: A three-tier production system for rating US equities — cloud ETL into a warehouse, a multi-factor quant model, and an async product backend serving the live app.
role: Backend engineer across all three tiers — ingestion, modelling and the product API.
doc:
Overview

FactorAlpha rates US equities. A cloud pipeline ingests fundamentals, prices and analyst estimates for over 5,000 tickers; a five-factor model scores around 2,900 of them and grades each one from Strong Buy to Strong Sell; and an async API serves those ratings, fair-value analytics and portfolio tools to the live app. I build all three parts.

What I did

  • Built the ingestion platform end to end, designed so any run can be safely repeated — recovering from a failure is just running it again.
  • Built the rating model. Each factor is weighted by how well it has actually predicted forward returns, re-estimated every quarter rather than fixed by theory.
  • Made the universe survivorship-bias-free by backfilling a decade of index membership, including names that have since delisted.
  • Built the product API behind the app, plus the scheduling and monitoring the whole thing runs on.

name: FinSight
short: The complete backend for a US equities and options trading app — order execution against a live brokerage, options analytics, portfolio monitoring, and the GenAI assistant on top.
sub: The entire Python backend for an algorithmic trading platform — 87 REST endpoints across 9 domain modules, wired to a live brokerage, plus the retrieval-augmented assistant.
role: Backend engineer — orders, market data, analytics and monitoring; built the GenAI core; led the runtime migration.
note: Internal product — happy to walk through it on a call.
doc:
Overview

FinSight is an algorithmic trading platform. I own the Python backend — orders and positions wired to a live brokerage, market data, analytics and monitoring, across 87 endpoints — and I built the retrieval-augmented assistant that answers questions about the platform and a user's own activity.

What I did

  • Built the order, position and analytics services against a live brokerage integration, where a bad write costs real money.
  • Built the GenAI core from scratch — retrieval, prompting and the answer path — at roughly 90% response accuracy.
  • Led a runtime migration of the backend that required no changes at all from the frontend team.

name: Rule AI
short: A no-code business rules engine for credit decisioning — analysts draw decision logic, chain it into workflow graphs, simulate it in bulk and publish it as a secured API. I built the backend.
sub: A no-code decision-management platform for lending and credit risk: visual rule authoring compiled into executable workflow graphs, bulk-simulated and published as production decision APIs.
role: Backend engineer — rule compiler, workflow DAG engine, bulk execution, caching, access control and governance.
note: Internal product — happy to walk through it on a call.
doc:
Overview

Rule AI lets lending and credit-risk teams write decision rules without writing code. Rules are authored visually, compiled into executable workflows, simulated in bulk against historical data, then published as production decision APIs. I built the backend: the compiler, the execution engine and the bulk-run path.

What I did

  • Built the compiler that turns authored rules into something executable, and the engine that runs them in the right order with dependencies resolved.
  • Built bulk simulation, so a team can test a policy change against a large historical set before publishing it. This is the piece that cut client workflow time by more than 95%.
  • Added the access control and change history a regulated lending workflow needs before anyone will sign off on it.

name: corestrat.ai — backend + AI chatbot
short: Two production services behind the company website: the public chat backend API, and the retrieval-augmented GenAI engine that answers from Corestrat's own document corpus.
sub: Two production services live on corestrat.ai — a public FastAPI backend handling chat traffic, sessions and conversation persistence, and the RAG engine it delegates answers to.
role: Principal author of the current RAG engine — pipeline, retrieval chain, production prompt, service layer, config and deployment. On the backend API: performance, background-task persistence, engine integration and a live database migration.
doc:
Overview

Two services sit behind corestrat.ai: the public chat backend, and the retrieval-augmented engine it hands questions to. I am the principal author of the engine — the pipeline, the retrieval, the production prompt and the deployment. On the backend API, which the team had already scaffolded, I did the performance work and the data layer.

What I did

  • Wrote the current engine: how documents are retrieved, how an answer gets composed, and the prompt it runs in production. Roughly 90% answer accuracy.
  • Took writes off the response path, so answering a question no longer waits on anything being saved first.
  • Ran a database migration against the service while it stayed up.

name: RawDiary
short: A journaling app with no login at all. Usernames resolve in the browser against a Bloom filter in under 10ms — no database call to check if a name is taken. 100+ concurrent users at $0/month.
sub: A stateless, zero-authentication journaling app. No accounts, no identity database — and it runs at $0/month.
role: All of it — the Next.js frontend, the FastAPI backend, caching, spatial queries, audio masking and deployment.
doc:
Overview

RawDiary is a journaling app with no accounts and no identity database. You pick a name and you write. It carries 100+ concurrent users at $0/month in infrastructure.

What I did

  • Username availability resolves in the browser against a Bloom filter in under 10ms — no database call to find out whether a name is taken.
  • Feeds are cursor-paginated out of Redis instead of re-queried each time.
  • Voice entries can be masked in the browser with the Web Audio API before they ever leave the device.
  • All of it is mine — design, frontend, backend, deploy.

name: VeinChain
short: Logging in with the veins in your finger. We built the infrared capture hardware ourselves and put the identity record on Ethereum instead of in a database. Became two working apps and a paper.
sub: Finger-vein biometric authentication with enrolment anchored on-chain, built on custom low-cost infrared capture hardware.
role: Smart contracts, backend, frontends and the capture hardware.
doc:
Overview

VeinChain authenticates a person by the vein pattern inside their finger. We built the infrared capture rig ourselves out of low-cost parts, and anchored the enrolment record on Ethereum rather than keeping biometrics in a central database. It became two working applications and a research paper.

What I did

  • Wrote the smart contracts that hold the enrolment records, so there is no central biometric store to breach.
  • Built the capture hardware and the image pipeline that turns a raw infrared frame into something matchable.
  • Built both applications on top, and co-wrote the paper.

A university project, built with classmates. The contracts, the backend and the capture pipeline were my part.

name: RAG-app
short: Ask questions about your own PDFs without anything leaving your laptop. LangChain pipeline running Llama 3 locally — zero API cost, and documents never travel.
sub: Retrieval-augmented question answering over your own documents, running entirely on your machine.
doc:
Overview

Ask questions about your own PDFs with nothing leaving your machine. A LangChain pipeline over Llama 3 running locally — no API key, no cost per question, and the documents never travel.

What I did

  • Built the whole local pipeline: chunking, embedding, retrieval and answering.
  • Added OCR so scanned PDFs work, not just text-native ones.
  • Shipped it with two front doors — an API and a UI.

name: EDU-AI
short: A learning platform that works out how you learn. A short survey infers VARK and MBTI style, a Random Forest classifier predicts it at 91% accuracy, and the material adapts to match.
sub: A personalised learning platform that infers how a student learns and reshapes the material to match.
role: Full stack — the Flask backend and MySQL data layer, the Random Forest classifier, the Gemini content generation and the interface.
doc:
Overview

EDU-AI works out how a student learns, then reshapes the material to match. A short survey infers VARK learning style and MBTI type, a Random Forest predicts it at 91% accuracy, and the content is regenerated in the format that suits.

What I did

  • Trained and tuned the classifier that predicts learning style, to 91% accuracy.
  • Built the Flask backend and the MySQL data layer.
  • Wired up Gemini for content generation and built the student-facing interface.

Built with three classmates. The backend, the classifier and the Gemini integration were mine.
